interest: Shows 1940 Soviet-US intelligence sharing in Tokyo on Japan's expanded northern 'fishery patrol' fleet near Kamchatka and the Kurils.
overview: 1940 naval attaché report: Smith-Hutton relays Soviet data on an unusually large Japanese 'fishery patrol' fleet of cruisers, destroyers, and submarines near the Kurils and Kamchatka, with Soviet suspicions of Japanese activity near Alaska.

people.name: Henri H. Smith-Hutton
people.role: Lieutenant Commander, U.S. Navy, Naval Attaché, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Intelligence report on an expanded Japanese naval force operating under the guise of fishery patrol in the Kuril Islands and Kamchatka area, based on information from the Soviet Naval Attaché in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: H.H. Smith-Hutton, Lt.-Comdr., U.S. Navy, Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Attaché report: Smith-Hutton cites Soviet intelligence on a large 1940 Japanese 'fishery patrol' force of cruisers, destroyers, and submarines near the Kurils and Kamchatka, suspected of also operating near Alaska.
subfiles.title: Attaché's Report No. 110: Japanese Naval Vessels in Kurile Island Area - Fishery Patrol
subfiles.to: Director of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department
